Sets the ambient light of a level, a color that is added to the light the level has, which is its lightmap or, with vertex lighting, the colors of its vertices. A new level starts at 0, 0, 0, so nothing is added. Levels ignore the normal [AmbientLight](AmbientLight), which is why this command exists. It can make a dark level easier to see, although using the gamma value of [LoadBSP](LoadBSP) looks nicer in the original. To multiply the level with a color instead, use [BSPLightmapColor](BSPLightmapColor).
@param bsp    The level.
@param red    Red part, 0 to 255.
@param green  Green part, 0 to 255.
@param blue   Blue part, 0 to 255.
@gap The original adds the color to the light of each face before the texture is applied, and lights the vertices of a level with point and spot lights too. Here the color is added after the lightmap and the texture, as the texture times the color, and no light affects a level, so the result is the same where a texture is white or missing and close otherwise. The color is not changed by [BSPLightmapColor](BSPLightmapColor).
